data.name: UploadLimits.Intro
data.value: Every model is checked against these before it is made.

data.name: UploadLimits.JoinedRegions
data.value: These are the limits of this computer's own regions. Regions on computers that joined the grid aren't checked, and one with stricter settings could refuse the item.

data.name: UploadLimits.LargestPart.Why
data.value: Regions refuse parts larger than this.

data.name: UploadLimits.LargestPart.Tip
data.value: In Blender, check the size in the N panel; scale down (S) and apply the scale (Ctrl+A).

data.name: UploadLimits.LargestPhysical.Why
data.value: Parts that move with physics must be smaller, so the region can work out collisions.

data.name: UploadLimits.LargestPhysical.Tip
data.value: In Blender, split a large model into smaller objects if it should be physical.

data.name: UploadLimits.SmallestPart.Why
data.value: Smaller parts can't be made, so they are left out.

data.name: UploadLimits.SmallestPart.Tip
data.value: In Blender, join tiny pieces to a larger part (Ctrl+J).

data.name: UploadLimits.Parts.Why
data.value: An item is a set of linked parts; regions can limit how many.

data.name: UploadLimits.Parts.Tip
data.value: In Blender, join objects (Ctrl+J) to use fewer parts.

data.name: UploadLimits.Materials.Why
data.value: Each part has at most 8 faces, one material each. More materials are split into extra linked parts for you.

data.name: UploadLimits.Materials.Tip
data.value: In Blender, join materials that share a picture, or bake them into one.

data.name: UploadLimits.Points.Why
data.value: Larger faces are split for you.

data.name: UploadLimits.Points.Tip
data.value: In Blender, a Decimate modifier lowers the number of points.

data.name: UploadLimits.Picture.Why
data.value: Pictures are resized to a power of two no larger than this, to keep the grid quick to load.

data.name: UploadLimits.Picture.Tip
data.value: In Blender, save pictures at 1024 × 1024 or smaller.

data.name: UploadLimits.Heavy.Why
data.value: Above this, the simpler versions shown from far away may look lumpy or have holes.

data.name: UploadLimits.Heavy.Tip
data.value: In Blender, add a Decimate modifier.

data.name: UploadLimits.Triangles.Why
data.value: The most this grid can take in one item.

data.name: UploadLimits.Triangles.Tip
data.value: In Blender, add a Decimate modifier.

data.name: UploadLimits.Objects.Why
data.value: The most this grid can take in one file.

data.name: UploadLimits.FileSize.Why
data.value: The largest file this grid takes.

data.name: UploadLimits.FileSize.Tip
data.value: In Blender, use smaller pictures; export as glTF Binary (.glb).

data.name: UploadLimits.PictureInFile.Why
data.value: Larger pictures aren't read at all.

data.name: UploadLimits.PictureInFile.Tip
data.value: In Blender, scale pictures down before exporting.

data.name: Finding.TooBig.Title

data.name: Finding.TooSmall.Why

data.name: Finding.TooSmall.Tip

data.name: Finding.TooManyParts.Why
data.value: This grid allows {0} parts in one item.

data.name: Finding.InsideOut.Why
data.value: It was mirrored, so its faces may point the wrong way and look see-through.

data.name: Finding.InsideOut.Tip

data.name: Finding.InsideOutMany.Why
data.value: It was mirrored, so its faces may point the wrong way and look see-through.

data.name: Finding.InsideOutMany.Tip
data.value: In Blender, apply the scale (Ctrl+A), then in Edit Mode recalculate the normals (Shift+N).

data.name: Finding.NoUv.Title
data.value: {0} faces have a picture but no UV map

data.name: Finding.NoUv.Why
data.value: Without one the picture can't be placed, so it will look smeared.

data.name: Finding.NoUv.Tip
data.value: In Blender, unwrap the mesh in Edit Mode (U), then export again.

data.name: Finding.DroppedAnimation.Why
data.value: Items here can't play glTF animations. This won't change how it looks standing still.

data.name: Finding.DroppedAnimation.Tip
data.value: Nothing to fix. In Blender's glTF export you can untick Animation.

data.name: Finding.DroppedMorphs.Why
data.value: The item is made in its basic shape.

data.name: Finding.DroppedMorphs.Tip
data.value: In Blender, apply the shape key you want before exporting, or untick Shape Keys in the glTF export.

data.name: Finding.DroppedExtras.Why
data.value: Items can't carry them. This won't change how it looks.

data.name: Finding.DroppedExtras.Tip
data.value: In Blender's glTF export, untick Cameras and Punctual Lights.

data.name: Finding.VertexColours.Title
data.value: The model's vertex colours were left out

data.name: Finding.VertexColours.Why
data.value: Items here can only take colour from a material or a picture, so it may look plainer.

data.name: Finding.VertexColours.Tip
data.value: In Blender, bake the vertex colours into a picture (Cycles: Bake, Diffuse colour), then export again.

data.name: Finding.DoubleSided.Title
data.value: {0} will only show from one side

data.name: Finding.DoubleSided.Why
data.value: Items here draw a face from the front only, so thin parts like leaves or cloth may look see-through from behind.

data.name: Finding.DoubleSided.Tip
data.value: In Blender, give thin parts some thickness with a Solidify modifier, then export again.

data.name: Finding.DoubleSidedMany.Title
data.value: {0} will only show from one side ({1} materials)

data.name: Finding.DoubleSidedMany.Why
data.value: Items here draw a face from the front only, so thin parts like leaves or cloth may look see-through from behind.

data.name: Finding.DoubleSidedMany.Tip
data.value: In Blender, give thin parts some thickness with a Solidify modifier, then export again.

data.name: Finding.TextureCoords.Title
data.value: A picture may sit in the wrong place

data.name: Finding.TextureCoords.Why
data.value: Only the model's first UV map is used, as it is; a second UV map or a moved or scaled picture is not.

data.name: Finding.TextureCoords.Tip
data.value: In Blender, put the picture on the first UV map and apply any offset or scale to the UVs, then export again.

data.name: Finding.SkinIgnored.Title

data.name: Finding.SkinIgnored.Tip
data.value: In Blender, export without the armature if you only want the object.

data.name: Finding.Compressed.Why
data.value: Compressed models can't be read here.

data.name: Finding.Compressed.Tip

data.name: Finding.ExternalFiles.Why

data.name: Finding.ExternalFiles.Tip

data.name: Finding.NotTriangles.Why

data.value: In Blender, use File > Export > glTF 2.0 and choose glTF Binary (.glb).
